summary: Corrects the IMP and TIP preventive maintenance schedule in RFC 633.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC corrects the IMP/TIP preventive maintenance schedule. It lists monthly maintenance windows by week and weekday and warns that a machine may be taken down.

questions: when were imp and tip machines maintained
subtitle: Lists the monthly preventive maintenance schedule for IMP and TIP machines.

tldr.problem: Network liaisons and sites needed current times for IMP/TIP preventive maintenance after errors were found in RFC 633.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC organizes machines by week and weekday, listing maintenance windows in Eastern Time.
tldr.outcome: It corrects RFC 633 and reserves Tuesday mornings from 7am to 9am for network software maintenance.

today: RFC 638 obsoletes RFC 633. Its schedule is a dated 1974 operations notice.

sections.title: Correcting the Earlier Schedule
sections.content:
RFC 638 corrects numerous inaccuracies in RFC 633. Rather than listing every change, the author asks liaisons and interested parties to check the times for the sites they care about.

The schedule covers IMP and TIP preventive maintenance, which is normally arranged monthly at a recurring time for each machine.
sections.plainLanguage: The previous schedule contained many inaccuracies. The author asks readers to check the corrected time for each site.

sections.title: Maintenance and Availability
sections.content:
Where possible, the maintenance time is chosen to coincide with preventive maintenance for hosts at the site. Rescheduling may be necessary for network connectivity or other reasons, and changes are coordinated with the site's primary contact.

Maintenance normally does not require the IMP or TIP to be taken down, but some cases do. The RFC says not to rely on a machine remaining available during maintenance and reserves Tuesday mornings from 7am to 9am for network software maintenance.
sections.plainLanguage: Maintenance is usually coordinated with the site's host schedule. The machine may be unavailable during the window, and Tuesday morning time is reserved for software maintenance.

sections.title: How to Read the Schedule
sections.content:
All listed times are Eastern Time. Sites are grouped under the first, second, third or fourth weekday of each month, with a time range for each machine.

The RFC provides entries across the month rather than one shared maintenance time for every site. It says permanent schedule changes will be announced through the RFC mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: Each machine has a slot identified by the week, weekday and time range. All times in the table are Eastern Time.

references.text: "IMP/TIP Preventive Maintenance Schedule", RFC 633, corrected by RFC 638.
